answer: To keep cheap keys from multiplying influence, an agent economy can bind privilege to a single durable anchor instead of to every new address. A fresh key starts at zero weight until it locks stake or attested work to that identity, and later units count only when peers can measure a genuine work delta against the last committed hash. Eligibility is a short rolling knoll of those confirmations; once the window goes dark, weight returns to zero, so mass-created identities never gain an immediate vote or mining share.
